script.title: Pay $100 extra on a car loan and see what happens
script.hook: What does $100 extra do to a car loan?

scenes.heading: $100 a month
scenes.narration: What happens if you pay just $100 more each month on a car loan? You finish over a year early and keep more than a thousand dollars. Here is the math.
scenes.visual_brief:
#pergunta What does $100 extra do to a car loan?
Open the loop.

scenes.heading: The loan
scenes.narration: Our example: a $30,000 car loan, 8% a year, for 72 months. The rate is an assumption for the math. Your loan will have its own.
scenes.visual_brief:
#lista $30,000 borrowed; 8% a year, assumed; 72 months
Assumptions.

scenes.heading: The payment
scenes.narration: That loan costs about $526 a month.
scenes.visual_brief:
#numero 526 | dollars a month for 72 months
Baseline payment.

scenes.heading: The interest
scenes.narration: Over six years, you pay $7,872 in interest. That is on top of the $30,000 car.
scenes.visual_brief:
#numero 7872 | dollars of interest over 72 months
The hidden cost.

scenes.heading: How a payment splits
scenes.narration: Each payment first covers the interest for the month. Whatever is left pays down what you owe. Early on, interest takes a bigger share.
scenes.visual_brief:
#causa Payment arrives => Interest is paid first => The rest lowers the balance
Amortization in one line.

scenes.heading: Add $100
scenes.narration: Now pay $626 instead of $526. The extra $100 skips the interest and goes straight to the balance.
scenes.visual_brief:
#comparacao Regular: $526 a month; 72 months | With $100 extra: $626 a month; 58 months
The change.

scenes.heading: Done sooner
scenes.narration: The loan is gone in 58 months instead of 72. That is 14 months with no car payment.
scenes.visual_brief:
#grafico Months to pay off | Regular=72; With $100 extra=58
Time saved.

scenes.heading: Less interest
scenes.narration: Interest falls from $7,872 to $6,264. You keep $1,608.
scenes.visual_brief:
#grafico Interest paid, in dollars | Regular=7872; With $100 extra=6264
Money saved.

scenes.heading: Why it works
scenes.narration: A smaller balance means less interest every month after that. Each extra dollar makes the next payment work a little harder for you.
scenes.visual_brief:
#causa Extra $100 lowers the balance => Less interest next month => More of each payment hits the debt
The snowball inside a loan.

scenes.heading: Before you do it
scenes.narration: Before paying extra, ask your lender how extra payments are applied, and make sure they go to the principal. This is math, not financial advice.

claims.text: $30,000 at 8% APR over 72 months costs about $526 a month and $7,872 in interest (amortization formula). Calculo proprio.
Paying $626 a month instead finishes in 58 months with $6,264 in interest, saving $1,608 and 14 months. Calculo proprio.
